intended_object: The absolute logarithmic (Weil) height h(x) = (1/[ℚ(x):ℚ]) · log ∏_v max(|x|_v,1)^{n_v} of an algebraic number x, with junk value 0 for non-algebraic elements. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the companion definition absMulHeight₁.
explanation: The body is Real.log (absMulHeight₁ x). For x integral over ℚ, absMulHeight₁ x is H_{ℚ(x)}(x)^{1/[ℚ(x):ℚ]}. Here H_K is the relative multiplicative height built from the number-field AdmissibleAbsValues instance: infinite places counted with multiplicity mult, finite places normalised so the product formula holds; lemma mulHeight₁_eq confirms this is the usual product over places. Its log is therefore (1/d)·log H_{ℚ(x)}(x), the standard absolute logarithmic height. Computing it in ℚ(x) is the standard choice, since the value does not depend on the number field containing x. For non-algebraic x, absMulHeight₁ returns 1, so absLogHeight₁ returns log 1 = 0, as its docstring says. Defining it on any characteristic-zero field is the natural generality for heights of algebraic numbers. Mathlib has relative heights (Height.logHeight₁) but no other definition of the absolute height.
